author: Mark Atwood
text:
Workspace-coordination decision spanning metadata-server, calendars-server (JMAP-ic0j.26), and tasks-server (JMAP-ops7.23). Filing human because (1) public-API-breaking trait change on three sibling crates; (2) JMAP-ic0j.26 is the parent workspace bead on this exact question and is still open; (3) the bead presents three non-equivalent patterns.

**Survey of current state (verified 2026-05-18):**
- filenode-server/src/backend.rs:355-362 — explicit reference pattern. Rustdoc cites workspace AGENTS.md "Filter algebra exclusion §1": "workspace policy treats silent-drop in a query result as a server-side correctness bug".
- metadata-server/src/backend.rs:201-218 — default impl drops filter_related_type / filter_metadata_type args via `let _ = (filter_related_type, filter_metadata_type)` and delegates to get_changes. memory.rs:1257-1354 OVERRIDES correctly (carries related_type / metadata_type per ChangeRecord, filters all three arrays).
- metadata-server/src/metadata.rs:174-244 — handler post-filters created+updated by re-fetching; destroyed is intentionally not post-filtered ("destroyed objects no longer exist") and metadata.rs:88-104 documents this as a default-impl limitation.

**Recommendation: option (a) — drop the default impl.** Rationale:
1. Workspace AGENTS.md "Filter algebra and control enums are explicitly EXCLUDED" §1 (silent-drop = server-side query-correctness bug) is the canonical workspace policy. Default impls that silently drop filter args are the same bug class.
2. filenode-server is already the reference pattern with explicit rustdoc citing this policy. Aligning metadata-server with filenode-server makes 2 of 8 extension-servers coherent (then calendars + tasks via JMAP-ic0j.26 / JMAP-ops7.23 complete the sweep).
3. The MemoryBackend reference impl ALREADY honors all three arrays (memory.rs:1257-1354), so dropping the trait default does not break the reference impl. The only thing it breaks is partial-compliance backends — which workspace policy says should not exist.
4. Pre-publish workspace: trait API breaks are cheap. Workspace consistency is high value.

Option (b) requires extending get_metadata_changes to return per-destroyed-id type metadata so the handler can filter, OR adding a new backend method. Either way it is functionally a trait API break, just structured differently. No real preservation benefit.

Option (c) preserves the workspace-policy-violating status quo. Not workable.

**Why not just do option (a) autonomously:** This is the parent decision on JMAP-ic0j.26 (open) and gates JMAP-ops7.23 (open). A single trait-shape decision needs to be made once and propagated to all three crates in a coordinated change set, not done piecemeal. The right vehicle is a workspace epic that owns the propagation; this bead can close out as superseded by that epic once it is filed.
